lines: West stair is deep survey and deep survey is not a floor, it is a directorate.
I do not have a list of who may go down. I have a list of who may not, and it is everybody.
Six coastal traces flat for nine weeks and I have been told it is the instruments.
I have replaced the instruments. Twice. With my own hands.
The sea off this coast is not moving, and nobody upstairs will write that down.
Thirty-one years of calling weather and I am still wrong one day in five.
The trick is to be wrong safely. Wrong towards the hill, never wrong towards the water.
Fourteen people and every night of next month covered, in case.
In case of what, is the question I am paid not to be able to answer.
Something has been ordering cold-weather kit in quantities I did not requisition.
Two species back off the edge and one gone while I was in this chair.
I keep the page. Everybody tells me to take it out of the register.
It stays in. If it stops hurting to read, I have stopped being any use.
Eleven miles a day, all of it indoors. I have worn out three pairs of boots in here.
Anything going west down that stair, I hand to the man at the top.
Anything coming back up it, there has never been any.
River mouths, monthly, all thirty-two of them. Salt, silt, temperature, the lot.
The eastern samples were all taken in the same week and stoppered, which is not monthly.
Somebody stopped going east. Nobody stopped writing the reports.
Aurelian resonance. Beautiful work, and none of it was built to push.
You put current into one of their rings and it does not do more. It goes quiet.
Like a person who has decided not to argue with you. I find that hard to be near.
You have a badge, so you may read, and I will sit here while you do it.
One rule and it is not mine: a file may leave this room for the Director's office and nowhere else.
In forty years, three have. I remember all three.
Requests in writing, pencil only, and nothing leaves this room.
Yes, that is a rule about paper. It is also the only rule in this building
that has ever been broken by somebody senior enough to break it.
Loss reports are the worst of it. A hull survey, a crew list, and a tick or a blank.
You get used to the blanks. What you do not get used to is a report
with no assessor's name at the bottom, because that means nobody went and looked.
